directions.name: As it stands
directions.thesis: The enclosure display as the firmware draws it today, transcribed to the pixel.
directions.why: The baseline every direction is compared against.

directions.name: Black Glass
directions.thesis: The panel is a sheet of black glass in the cabinet face, and nothing is drawn on it — things are lit behind it.
directions.why: Attacks the pressure that a kitchen appliance must disappear when it is not being used and be unambiguous when it is. Cards, borders and badges are graphic-design furniture; a Gaggenau or a Sub-Zero says everything with light and dark on one continuous black surface, so the panel reads as part of the cabinetry rather than as a tablet glued to it. It buys enormous calm and makes the two saturated faces the only objects on screen. It costs the reassurance of drawn containers: a user who expects buttons has to learn that a lit field is a target, and the near-black steps have to survive a lit kitchen.
directions.references: Gaggenau 400 series black-glass fascia, Miele Generation 7 M Touch, Bang & Olufsen Beosound, Sub-Zero panel-ready integrated fronts, a Vitrifrigo/Liebherr wine cabinet's readout.
directions.palette: background #060708, surface #0e1113, surface-alt #171b1e, accent #7ed0e0 (cold indicator light, used only on the active rail bar, the selection rule and the progress light), secondary #2c3438 (hairlines, unlit glyph strokes), text #f2f5f6, text-dim #7c878c, good #3fbf8f, warn #e8a23a. Every fill is flat — no gradient anywhere, because three near-black steps are already close to what RGB565's 5-bit blue can separate. Each ground step differs by at least 8 in the 8-bit green channel so the ladder survives quantisation.
directions.typography: Inter Tight from Google Fonts, weights 300/400/600. Hierarchy is size and tracking, never colour: page name 22px/600 uppercase, tracking 0.18em, text; section captions 20px/600 uppercase, tracking 0.16em, text-dim; body 20px/400; ratio numerals 64px/300 with tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) so 1:20 and 1:14 occupy identical width under the −/+; lock title 44px/400; the minutes figure 28px/600. No weight above 600 anywhere — bold is what cheap panels use to shout.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190 + 610 skeleton and dissolves what fills it. The rail has no cards: each 190×110 cell is bare background carrying a 44px glyph stroked 2px in secondary over a 20px word in text-dim; the active cell alone gets a 4×64px accent bar flush to x=0 and its glyph and word step to text. One 2px #1b2023 seam at x=190 is the only line on the panel. In the pane, cards are replaced by lit fields: a region that matters is #0e1113 on #060708, with 24px of air instead of a border. Settings is a 48px gear outlined 2px in secondary in the top-right corner, no field behind it. On settings, the side profile is drawn as a 2px secondary outline of the enclosure on bare background; a closed reed is a 14px filled good disc, an open one a 14px ring stroked 2px in secondary — filled-versus-empty plus a hue step, separable at two metres.
directions.selectionDevice: Light. The selected flavor's field steps from background to surface-alt #171b1e and carries a 3px accent rule across its full width at its bottom edge; the unselected flavor's field stays at background with no rule and its face composited over a 45% black veil, so it visibly sits behind the glass while the other sits on it. No badge and no word: one region is lit and the other is not, which is the same language the rail's active bar speaks.
directions.faceTreatment: 43:80, 4px radius, a 1px #2a3135 hairline so the face's own dark edge does not bleed into the ground. Choose: 148×275 per card, standing at the card's west. Flavor page and every pick: 172×320 anchored at the pane's west edge under the back key. The picker row runs eight 64×119 faces at 12px pitch with the chosen one carrying a 3px accent underline and a 4px accent hairline inset on its frame; the row sits over a 4px track at #171b1e with an accent thumb, and 56×96 chevron keys at either end lit text when they can travel and secondary when they cannot.
directions.lockTreatment: No animation loop. The panel goes to solid background, the channel's face at 129×240 stands at the west, and progress is one 610×6px light bar at surface-alt filling accent from the left; a 60px brighter accent segment travels inside the unfilled remainder at 10 fps (the still frame shows fill at 40% with the segment at 58%). Above it, `Cleaning` 44px; below, `1 of 3 · water in` 20px dim and `11 MIN LEFT` 20px uppercase tracked in accent. STOP is a 220×88 field outlined 2px in secondary with text at 20px/600 — the only outlined object on the whole direction, which is what makes it read as the one way out.
directions.risks: In a lit kitchen an IPS panel's black floor is charcoal, so #060708/#0e1113/#171b1e can collapse into one grey — the 3px accent rule and the veiled face have to carry selection on their own if it does. RGB565 gives blue only 32 levels, so the cold accent must be checked at the panel's own quantisation. 1px hairlines seen from above at arm's length disappear; nothing structural may be thinner than 2px. A fully black panel behind glass is a mirror of the kitchen ceiling light and a fingerprint museum.

directions.name: Milled Face
directions.thesis: The panel is not a screen pretending to be a panel — it is the machined aluminium fascia of the appliance, with pockets milled into it and one indicator lamp lit.
directions.why: Attacks the pressure that a touch panel next to a Wolf hob or a Vola tap reads as the cheapest object in the kitchen because everything on it is drawn rather than made. Material honesty here means the opposite of flat design: chamfers, milled troughs, engraved labels and a real indicator bead, all built from flat fills and 2px edges so RGB565 never bands. It buys the sense that the controls are machined into the same billet as the rest of the machine, and it gives the panel a mid-value ground that is neither a nightlight nor a black mirror. It costs contrast headroom: a grey ground leaves less room for a dim caption than black or bone does.
directions.references: Wolf induction control fascia, Thermomix TM6 bezel, Miele stainless fronts, Leica and Linhof bodies, Teenage Engineering OP-1, Buchla panel engraving, Vola tap hardware.
directions.palette: background #3b3e40 (the anodized face plate), surface #565a5d (a milled pocket floor), surface-alt #2b2e30 (a machined trough, and the dark chamfer), accent #34b6b9 (anodized teal indicator — beads, active engraving fill, progress), secondary #9aa0a3 (engraved label grey), text #eef0f1, text-dim #a3a9ac, good #63c48d, warn #e9a13c. Chamfers are the material: 2px #6e7276 on the top and left of a raised body, 2px #2b2e30 on its bottom and right, inverted for a pocket. Brush is two flat colours, never a gradient — 1px rows alternating #565a5d and #5b5f62 at an exact 2px pitch on the panel's own grid.
directions.typography: Archivo from Google Fonts, 400/500/600, plus Archivo's tabular figures for every number. Labels are engraved rather than printed: text at 20px/600 uppercase tracked 0.14em in secondary with a 1px #2b2e30 copy offset +1px in y behind it, which is what makes a label read as cut into metal at arm's length. Page name 24px/600 tracked 0.16em in text. Ratio numerals 64px/500 tabular. Lock title 40px/600 tracked 0.12em. Nothing italic, nothing below 20px.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190 + 610 skeleton and machines it. The rail becomes a recessed trough: the left 190px sits at surface-alt with a 2px #6e7276 chamfer down x=188..190, and each destination is a 166×102 milled pocket at surface, inset chamfered, carrying a 44px glyph and an engraved word. A 12px indicator bead at each pocket's top-right is #23262a ringed 2px dark when idle and accent with a 1px #9fe6e8 core when active. The pane is the face plate at background with the brushed rows running across it. Settings is a 48×48 pocket in the top-right corner — recessed rather than raised, which is how a service control is distinguished from a use control. On settings, the side profile is engraved: a 2px #2b2e30 line with a 1px #6e7276 highlight offset −1px in y, so it reads as scribed into the plate; closed reeds are 14px accent-cored beads, open ones 14px #2b2e30 pockets with a 2px #6e7276 upper chamfer.
directions.selectionDevice: An indicator lamp and a blanked plate, exactly as an oven marks a live zone. The selected flavor's card is a lit pocket — floor steps to surface, a 16px accent bead with a 2px #2b2e30 ring sits at its top-right, and a 4px accent line runs the full height of the pocket's left inner wall. The unselected flavor is a blanked plate: floor at surface-alt, bead a dark #23262a ring with no core, type at text-dim. One lamp on, one off, plus a lit wall — unmistakable from two metres and from an angle.
directions.faceTreatment: 43:80 inlaid behind a cutout: a 3px inverted chamfer around the face (dark #2b2e30 top and left, light #6e7276 bottom and right) so the face sits below the plate rather than on it. Choose: 129×240 at the pocket's west. Flavor page and both pick cards: 172×320 anchored west under a milled back key of the same width. The picker row is eight 60×112 faces separated by 2px #2b2e30 seams inside one continuous milled strip — a single machined slot, not eight chips — with the chosen one wearing a 12px accent bead centred 10px above it and 3px accent chamfers on its own left and right seams. Beneath the strip a 6px trough at surface-alt with an accent thumb; the two 56×96 travel keys are raised plates that drop to surface-alt with #6e7276 glyphs when they cannot travel.
directions.lockTreatment: A machine readout, not an illustration. The pane becomes one wide milled channel: a 560×28 trough at surface-alt with a 2px inverted chamfer, filled accent to 40% with a 3px #9fe6e8 leading edge, and a single 20px accent bead travelling inside the unfilled remainder at 10 fps (still frame: fill at 40%, bead at 62%). Channel's face 129×240 inlaid at the west. `CLEANING` engraved at 40px; `1 OF 3 · WATER IN` 20px engraved in secondary; `11 MIN LEFT` 28px in accent. STOP is the one raised body on the screen — a 240×96 plate at #6e7276 with a 3px chamfer and 24px/600 text — so among pockets and troughs the exit is the only thing standing proud of the plate.
directions.risks: The 2px brushed pitch must never be scaled: rendered at dpr 2 and downsampled, or stretched by a layout engine, it moirés into visible bands on the real panel. A mid-grey ground caps the contrast ratio, so text-dim must not go below #a3a9ac and engraved labels must be checked against a lit kitchen's reflections rather than a dark bench. 2px chamfers are near the visibility floor at arm's length from above — the whole material illusion may simply not read, leaving a grey panel. Cool grey next to warm kitchen LEDs looks dirty; if the kitchen's lighting is 2700K, the plate may want a half-step warmer (#3d3f3f → #3f4040). Teal against flavor_2's green is the one adjacency to check.

directions.name: Bronze Fascia
directions.thesis: The controls belong on the appliance's own fascia along the bottom edge, and the panel above them is a lit stage where the two drinks stand.
directions.why: Attacks two pressures at once. First, a 43:80 face is a tall object and the 190px rail takes width away from exactly the axis the faces do not have to spare; moving the destinations to a bottom band gives a 768×344 stage where two faces stand at full size with real air between them. Second, on a 45° facet read from above by a standing adult, the panel's bottom edge is the edge nearest the reaching hand, which is where every built-in appliance in this kitchen puts its controls. It buys stage width and hand ergonomics, and a warm dark palette that sits with wood, bronze and stone rather than against them. It costs 104px of height, and it breaks the left-rail convention the faucet display shares.
directions.references: Gaggenau Vario and the warm side of the 400 series, La Cornue, Officine Gullo brass, Wolf's bronze knob program, Sub-Zero designer-series walnut fronts, Bang & Olufsen brass-and-oak.
directions.palette: background #14120f (warm near-black), surface #201c17 (a lit card), surface-alt #2b251d (pressed, and hairline frames), accent #c39b4a (brass — the active key, the selection rule, the time left, nothing else), secondary #6a5f4e (hairlines), text #f0e9dd (bone), text-dim #9c9082, good #7fa86a (sage), warn #d08a3c. Flat fills; the only 'sheen' permitted is a 1px #6a5f4e top edge on a brass rule.
directions.typography: Marcellus 400 from Google Fonts for page names and the lock title, set in caps tracked 0.10em and never smaller than 26px — a quiet roman capital is the type a hand-built appliance's nameplate wears. Jost 300/400/500 for everything else: ratio `1:20` at 72px/300 tabular (thin geometric numerals read as expensive and as precise), captions 20px/500 uppercase tracked 0.16em, body 20px/400, `11 MIN LEFT` 32px/400 in brass. Two families, two jobs, no exceptions.
directions.layoutMove: The rail leaves the left edge. A 800×104 fascia band sits at y=376 on #0e0c0a with a 2px brass hairline along its top edge; four 200px keys are divided by 1px #2b251d seams, each a 30px 2px-stroked glyph over a 20px/500 word. The active key steps its field to surface, takes its glyph and word to brass, and carries a 3px brass bar along the band's top edge across its own 200px only. Above, the stage runs y=0..376 with 20px gutters: a 56px title line, then content. Choose puts two 360×288 cards with a 40px gap. Settings is a 44px brass hairline gear in the stage's top-right, never in the band, because the band is the four customer destinations and nothing else. On settings, the side profile is a 2px secondary line drawing filling the stage's width; a closed reed is a 14px filled good disc, an open one a 14px ring in #6a5f4e.
directions.selectionDevice: Elevation plus a brass foot. The selected card sits at surface, is 8px taller than its neighbour (its top edge rises above the other card's), carries a 3px brass rule across its full bottom edge and sets its ratio in brass; the unselected sits on background inside a 1px surface-alt frame at the shorter height with all type at text-dim. Two cards of different height on one line is a silhouette difference, which is what survives a glance from two metres and an oblique angle better than any colour change.
directions.faceTreatment: 43:80, 2px radius, inside a 1px #6a5f4e frame — a warm hairline around a saturated face on warm near-black reads as a lit label on a bronze machine. Choose: 129×240 at each card's west, with the ratio and the four-segment gauge in the column east of it. Flavor page and both pick cards: 172×320 anchored at the stage's west under a back key of the same width. The picker row is eight 60×112 faces at 16px pitch on a #0e0c0a strip inset into the stage; the chosen one is lifted 6px above the row's baseline and framed 2px brass — again a silhouette cue, matching the selection language on Choose. A 4px surface-alt track with a brass thumb runs beneath; the travel keys are 56×88 brass hairline chevrons that go #3a3228 when they cannot travel.
directions.lockTreatment: The fascia goes dark. All four keys unlight, the seams and the brass top hairline disappear, and the band becomes flat #0e0c0a carrying one thing: a 240×72 key outlined 2px brass reading STOP, centred. The stage above holds the channel's face at 129×240 west, `CLEANING` in Marcellus 48px bone, and progress read as weight rather than fill — a hairline that is 2px #6a5f4e across the whole cycle and thickens to 8px brass across the completed 40%, with the step between them as the leading edge. `1 of 3 · water in` 20px dim beneath; `11 MIN LEFT` 32px brass above. The one moving element is a 2-second brass pulse on the 8px leading edge, no loop and no illustration: the machine at work is the least decorated the panel ever gets, and the only way out is where every control already lives.
directions.risks: The bottom band is the region most likely to be occluded by a countertop overhang, a hand holding a glass, or the user's own forearm while reaching down over the facet — the install envelope has to be checked before this skeleton is committed. Brass #c39b4a sits close in hue to warn #d08a3c; the two must never appear in the same card, and LOW may need the sage/amber pair re-tuned. Brass against flavor_2's green is a muddy adjacency. Marcellus below 26px is unreadable at arm's length, so no caption may ever use it. A warm near-black shows an IPS panel's off-state glow as brown in a dark room. And the destinations moving off the left edge means the enclosure and the faucet no longer place the same controls in the same place.

directions.name: Cold Slab
directions.thesis: A white slab of cold stone with the drink set into it — the only colour on this panel is the soda, and everything else is carried by value, weight and elevation.
directions.why: Attacks the pressure that the flavor faces are the one thing the user is actually looking for, and that every accent colour an interface adds competes with them. Refusing hue entirely — except one burnt amber reserved for a low reservoir — makes the two faces the only chromatic objects on 384,000 pixels, which is the strongest possible selection cue and needs no badge. A cold near-white also puts the panel in the same family as a Miele front or a Sub-Zero interior, and reads well in daylight from above, which is where this panel is actually read. It costs night comfort and demands real discipline: with no hue to lean on, every state has to be built from weight, size, fill and elevation.
directions.references: Miele Generation 7 white, Sub-Zero interior lighting and shelving, Bosch white fascia, Vola and Dornbracht spec drawings, Braun ET66-era value hierarchies, Leitz microscope panels.
directions.palette: background #e7ebee (pale glacial), surface #f7f9fa (the white slab), surface-alt #d5dbdf (the recessed field), accent #101619 (ink — the accent role is carried by full-strength ink and solid fills, not by a hue), secondary #58636a, text #101619, text-dim #7c878e, good #1d4b3a (a pine so deep it reads as ink at two metres and as a colour up close), warn #b4571c (burnt amber, the single hue on the panel, reserved for LOW and for nothing else). Rules are 2px #cfd6da; fills are flat.
directions.typography: One family: Archivo from Google Fonts, 400/600/800, with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` throughout. The whole hierarchy is size and weight. Page name 22px/600 uppercase tracked 0.20em in ink. Captions 20px/600 uppercase tracked 0.14em in text-dim. Body 20px/400. Ratio `1:20` at 72px/800 — the heaviest thing on the panel, because on this direction weight is what accent colour would otherwise be. `LOW` at 20px/800 in warn. Lock title 48px/700. `11 MIN LEFT` 28px/800. Nothing is italic and nothing is coloured to carry meaning except LOW.
directions.layoutMove: The rail narrows from 190 to a 96px pictogram gutter, buying the pane 114px. Four 96×110 cells, each a 44px pictogram stroked 3px; the three idle ones are #7c878e outlines on background, the active one is a solid ink glyph on a #f7f9fa slab that extends 8px into the pane as a physical tab, with a 2px #cfd6da rule at x=96 broken where the tab crosses it. No words in the gutter — the pane's own title already names the destination, so the word was printed twice. Settings is a 44px ink gear stroked 3px in the pane's top-right. On settings, the side profile is a 3px ink line drawing on a white slab, dimension-drawing in character; a closed reed is a 16px filled ink disc (good pine only at close range), an open one a 16px ring stroked 3px in #9aa5ac — fill versus ring at 16px is the one reed cue that works with no hue.
directions.selectionDevice: Elevation and weight, three cues stacked. The selected flavor stands on a #f7f9fa slab 12px taller and 12px wider than its neighbour, capped by a 6px solid ink bar across its full top edge, with its ratio set at 800 weight in ink. The unselected sits directly on the background with no slab, a 2px #cfd6da frame, and every piece of its type at 400 weight in #7c878e. One white block with a black cap next to flat pale grey — silhouette, value and weight all saying the same thing, with no hue spent.
directions.faceTreatment: 43:80 at 0 radius inside a 2px #c7ced3 frame — the frame matters here, because a face's own light edge would otherwise dissolve into the near-white slab. The narrowed gutter pays for scale: Choose runs 172×320 faces, the largest of any direction, so the two drinks are the panel's subject rather than its illustration. Flavor page and both pick cards keep 172×320 anchored at the pane's west under a back key of the same width. The picker row is eight 60×112 faces at 16px pitch; the chosen one stands on its own 8px-taller white slab with a 6px ink cap, the same device as Choose, so selection means one thing on every screen. A 4px #cfd6da track with an ink thumb runs beneath, and the 56×88 travel keys are ink chevrons that drop to #cfd6da when they cannot travel.
directions.lockTreatment: The slab fills with ink. The pane becomes one #f7f9fa slab inset 16px, and the operation's progress is the slab itself being consumed from the left: 40% of its width is solid ink #101619, and every element the boundary crosses inverts — the type, the face's frame, the STOP key — implemented as two identical copies of the content, the lower in ink-on-white and the upper in white-on-ink clipped to the filled region. The channel's face at 129×240 sits at the west, already inside the ink, framed 2px in #f7f9fa. `CLEANING` 48px/700, `1 of 3 · water in` 20px/600, `11 MIN LEFT` 28px/800. STOP is a 240×88 key with a 3px frame sitting in the bottom-right, the last region the fill reaches, and it inverts with the same clip so it is legible on either side of the boundary. No loop, no illustration: the moving thing is the panel being eaten by the job.
directions.risks: A near-white 800×480 at a backlight that cannot dim is a lamp in a dark kitchen — this is the direction's real cost and there is no PWM to soften it. The inverting clip is genuine firmware work in LVGL: two label sets plus a clipped container, redrawn as the boundary advances, on a panel where repaint area is the frame budget — it must be prototyped before this direction is chosen. With hue gone, reed state rests entirely on fill-versus-ring, so the dots must not go below 16px and the ring must be 3px. Burnt amber is the only hue, so a future face in that family would compete with LOW. And pale cool grey under warm 2700K kitchen light casts slightly blue against a white cabinet front — check the panel beside the actual enclosure finish.

directions.name: Cold Slab
directions.thesis: This panel is the glass door of a cold case at night: the drink is desirable because it is cold, so the whole screen is refrigerated and the only warmth on it is the flavor itself.
directions.why: It attacks appetite through temperature rather than through sweetness — cold is the one thing this machine does that a can in a pantry does not, and the panel can say so before a word is read. A near-black cool ground makes the two faces the only saturated objects on the glass, which is exactly the hierarchy the brief wants (the face is the name). It costs night-legibility margin: a dark panel in a sunlit kitchen goes grey and flat, and there is no backlight step between on and off to recover it, so every contrast in the sheet is sized for the washed-out case.
directions.references: Coca-Cola Freestyle's dark surround with lit flavor lozenges; a supermarket cold-case door with condensation running on the inside; Bevi's cool restraint; the frosted-bottle photography on a Stella or Coors cold-activated can; Sub-Zero and Gaggenau's habit of letting a lit interior be the only colour.
directions.palette: background #05080e, surface #0d1420, surface-alt #16202f, accent #58d7ff (ice cyan), secondary #1f4e63 (cold steel, for rules, tracks and inactive bars), text #eef6fb, text-dim #7d93a6, good #3fd6a0, warn #ffb03a
directions.typography: Oswald 500/600 for anything large — the ratio numeral at 64px 600, page and lock titles at 34px 500 uppercase with 0.08em tracking. IBM Plex Sans 400/600 for everything at or under 24 — labels 20px 600 uppercase 0.14em, body 22px 400. Hierarchy is carried by width and case, not by colour: Oswald's condensation lets a 64px numeral and a 20px label share a column without the label shrinking below the panel's floor. Nothing is set in the cyan accent except a single-word kicker.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190px rail and 610px pane exactly. The rail stops being cards and becomes the cooler's door jamb: one solid #0d1420 column, a 2px #1f4e63 rule at x 188, four full-width 110px bands separated by 1px hairlines, each an icon over a word. The active band is #16202f with a 6px #58d7ff bar hard on its left edge at x 0. The pane then runs edge to edge in #05080e with no card behind the page — only the two flavor panes are lit objects on it.
directions.selectionDevice: The selected flavor is behind clear glass, the other behind frost. Selected: full-saturation face, a 3px #58d7ff frame, a 1px white specular streak across the top-left of the pane, and an 8px #58d7ff bar the full card width on its floor. Unselected: the same geometry with a flat #0d1420 wash at 55% over the face and a 2px-pitch checkerboard of #16202f dithered across it — no frame, no bar, numerals in #7d93a6. From two metres one card is lit and one is fogged.
directions.faceTreatment: 43:80 at 129×240 on Choose, 172×320 on a flavor's own page, 86×160 in the picker and lock, each inset 4px inside a 1px #2a3a4d frame that reads as the glass in front of it. Condensation is drawn over the frame, never over the artwork: roughly forty hard-edged circles 3–6px in two flat colours, #1b2836 and #24384a, clustered in the bottom third. On a frosted (unselected) face those same beads render in #7d93a6 as frozen flecks. No blur, no alpha gradient — RGB565 would band either.
directions.lockTreatment: The 16-frame bubble loop is replaced by a frost cycle. The full 800×480 field frosts inward from all four edges in a four-step dithered ice mask (four flat tints between #05080e and #16202f, 2px checkerboard boundaries), with the channel's 172×320 face standing clear in the middle of it — the machine is visibly cold and working. Progress is a single 800×6 bar pinned to the screen's bottom edge, #58d7ff for the elapsed 40% and #1f4e63 for the rest, with no track chrome. Words sit right of the face: 11 MIN LEFT (IBM Plex 600 20, #58d7ff), Cleaning (Oswald 500 34), 1 of 3 · water in (IBM Plex 400 22, #7d93a6). STOP is a 200×72 #16202f plate with a 2px #58d7ff border, bottom right. Still frame: frost at 40%.
directions.risks: A near-black 800×480 in a lit kitchen loses most of its apparent contrast and will show the panel's own backlight bleed at the bezel — the reason no meaning is carried by anything darker than #16202f. Condensation beads under 3px read as dead pixels or dirt at arm's length, so the count stays low and the size stays up. #58d7ff on #05080e is the strongest pair available and will fringe on RGB565 at small stroke widths, so it never sets body text and never draws a 1px line. The frost mask is four flat tints on purpose; anyone who replaces it with a real gradient gets visible bands across the whole lock screen.

directions.name: Tap House
directions.thesis: A soda on tap is a bar order, so this panel is the back bar: the two flavors are tap handles, choosing one is pulling it, and the machine's own state is read off a brass gauge.
directions.why: It attacks the belongs-in-a-home pressure head on — warm walnut and brass is furniture language, and a $7,500 hand-built appliance under a counter is closer to a bar back than to a dispenser. Making the flavor a physical handle gives the selection a metaphor that reads at two metres without a badge or a checkmark, and gives the machine's busy state a gauge instead of a spinner. The cost is that warm dark browns compress fast: brass and walnut sit close in luminance, so the palette needs a hard minimum separation everywhere, and there is no room for a third warm colour.
directions.references: A pub back bar's brass rail and engraved plates; Perlick and Krome tap towers; the enamel-and-brass badges on a cask tap handle; pressure gauges on a CO2 regulator, which this machine actually has in the cabinet; the printed bar list of a good cocktail room.
directions.palette: background #241a12 (walnut), surface #33261a (lifted plate), surface-alt #1a120c (engraved recess), accent #d2a24c (brass), secondary #7d5a34 (dull bronze, for rules, bevels and inactive tracks), text #f4ece0 (cream), text-dim #a9967c, good #7fb069, warn #e0913a
directions.typography: Playfair Display 700 for anything 30px and up — the ratio numeral at 60px, page titles at 36px, the lock's operation word at 44px. Work Sans 500/600 for everything at or under 24 — labels 20px 600 uppercase 0.12em, body 22px 400. The split is not stylistic: Playfair's hairlines vanish on RGB565 below about 30px, so the rule is absolute — Playfair never appears small, Work Sans never appears large. Numerals are Playfair's lining figures, which is what makes 1:20 read as a bar list and not a readout.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190/610 skeleton, and turns the rail into an actual brass rail: a #1a120c column with a 4px #d2a24c vertical bar running the full 480 at x 184, and four 170×104 engraved plates in #33261a with a two-tone bevel (1px #00000040 on the top and left, 1px #d2a24c at 20% on the bottom and right — flat, not a gradient). The active plate is filled solid #d2a24c with #241a12 text and icon: a plate polished bright while the others stay dull.
directions.selectionDevice: The tap is pulled. The selected flavor's card sits 8px higher and 6px further left than its neighbour, wears a 4px #d2a24c collar all round, and grows a drawn brass shank and spout below it in SVG — 16px wide, 40px tall, ending in a 20px nozzle. The unselected card is square in its slot, collar 1px #7d5a34, no shank, field #241a12 against the selected card's #33261a. One handle is gold-ringed and standing proud of the rail; the other is parked.
directions.faceTreatment: The 43:80 face is the handle's badge. It is mounted in a 6px brass frame with 10px corners, a 1px cream hairline just inside the brass, and two 8px #d2a24c rivet discs centred on the top and bottom edges. Nothing is ever drawn over the artwork. Scales 129×240 on Choose, 172×320 on the anchored pages, 86×160 in the picker strip and on the lock's brass mounting plate.
directions.lockTreatment: A brass pressure gauge replaces the bubble loop. A 300px dial at x 40: face #1a120c, a #7d5a34 tick ring of 24 marks, cream numerals only at the two ends, a #d2a24c needle at 40% of a 240° sweep, and a red-line arc from 85–100% in #8c3b2e. The channel's 86×160 face sits on a brass plate below the dial. Right of it: CLEANING in Playfair 700 44, 1 of 3 · water in in Work Sans 400 22 #a9967c, and 11 MIN LEFT engraved in Work Sans 600 20 #241a12 on a 200×40 #d2a24c strip. STOP is a 200×72 #8c3b2e button with a 2px cream border. The needle is the only thing that moves; still frame at 40%.
directions.risks: Walnut, bronze and brass are three steps on one ramp and will collapse into one brown if the backlight is the only light in the room — every adjacent pair in the sheet needs a real luminance gap, and #7d5a34 must never carry text. Playfair below 30px is unreadable on this panel, which is a rule a later contributor will break by reusing a title style on a caption. Bar language drifts toward mancave: no leather grain, no scrollwork, no beer iconography, no dark-wood photographic texture — the walnut is a flat fill, and the only ornament is the rivets and the rail.

directions.name: Flavor Flood
directions.thesis: The person at this panel is choosing a drink, not operating an appliance — so the drink's own colour should own the glass, edge to edge, and everything else should be ink on paper.
directions.why: It attacks the two-metre selection problem with the largest instrument available: 480×384 of saturated colour against paper is a state change nobody can misread, and it needs no badge, ring or check to carry it. Flat colour fields are the best case for RGB565 and the best case for glare. It costs the direction all subtlety — there is no third level of emphasis, every screen has exactly one loud object, and a flavor whose declared colour runs dark puts a near-black slab next to white.
directions.references: Contemporary craft-soda can graphics — Olipop, Poppi, Recess — where the flavour is one flat field and one word; Pepsi's 2023 flat-colour system; Sanpellegrino's single-colour cans; Swiss poster printing, where the colour is the image.
directions.palette: background #faf7f1 (paper), surface #ffffff, surface-alt #eae4d9, accent — the channel's own declared colour, shipped in the sheet as --chan-a #c2213f and --chan-b #3faa2b (drawn off flavor_1's crimson and flavor_2's green; in firmware one hex is stored beside each logo), secondary #14110d (ink, which is the direction's second colour), text #14110d, text-dim #7a7268, good #1f8a54, warn #d1741a
directions.typography: Bricolage Grotesque 800 for the one loud object per screen — the ratio numeral at 72px, the lock headline at 96px, tracking −0.02em. Inter Tight 500/700 for everything else, and everything else is 20 or 24px: labels 20px 700 uppercase 0.06em, body 24px 500. There is no middle size in this direction on purpose. Nothing is set in a flavor colour on paper; flavor colour is a field, ink is the type, and reversed-out paper type is what appears on a field.
directions.layoutMove: The rail leaves the left edge and becomes a 96px bar across the full 800 at the screen's bottom — four 200×96 targets, a 40px icon left of the word, ink on paper, the active one filled #14110d and reversed to paper, with a 3px ink rule along the bar's top edge. This earns the change twice: a colour field has to reach three edges to be a field rather than a coloured box, which a 610px pane cannot do; and on a panel tilted back under a counter and read from above, the thumb arrives from below, so the destinations sit where the hand is and the drink sits where the eye is. The content area is 800×384 with a 24px gutter, and Settings stays a 64px square at the top right.
directions.selectionDevice: The flood itself. The selected flavor owns a full-bleed 480×384 field of its own colour running to the screen's top and left edges, with its face and its numbers reversed out in paper. The unselected flavor is a 272×384 white card with a 3px ink keyline, its face at full colour and its numbers in ink. The two are not the same size, the same ground or the same colour space — one is a poster, the other is a listing. A tap swaps which one is flooded.
directions.faceTreatment: On the flood the 43:80 face is placed at 172×320 hard against the field with no frame, no keyline and no radius, so the artwork looks poured out of the panel it sits on. On the white card it takes a 3px ink keyline at 129×240. Zero corner radius everywhere in the direction — every card, button and field is a printed rectangle. The picker strip on a flavor's own page is eight 86×160 faces on paper, ink keylines, the chosen one on a full-bleed band of its own colour with the face reversed into it.
directions.lockTreatment: The flood is the progress bar, at 800px long. The whole screen is the channel's colour from x 0 to x 320 (40%) and paper #faf7f1 from x 320 to x 800 — one hard vertical edge, no track, no percentage, no bar furniture. CLEANING is set in Bricolage 800 at 96px on a baseline at y 300, running across the split and changing colour at it: paper where it lies on the field, the field's colour where it lies on paper. The split point is the progress. The channel's 172×320 face stands at x 48 inside the field. 1 of 3 · water in and 11 MIN LEFT sit in Inter Tight 700 24 at y 360. STOP is a 260×88 ink rectangle at the bottom right with paper text, clear of the bottom bar, which is hidden while the lock is up. Still frame: the edge at x 320.
directions.risks: A dark declared flavor colour — a cola — puts 480px of near-black beside paper and glares; the sheet needs a stated luminance floor for --chan-* and a rule that reversed paper type only runs on colours below it. Moving the rail to the bottom on a back-tilted panel puts it under the heel of the hand, so a palm resting on the glass can land on CLEAN: the targets are 96 tall and the destructive ones still take their confirm page, but this is the direction's real cost. The flood is also the direction closest to a vending machine face, and the only things holding it back are the paper ground and the ink type — one bevel, glow or gradient collapses it, and a gradient across a field that size would band on RGB565 anyway.

directions.name: Inside The Glass
directions.thesis: The screen is not a control surface with a drink on it — the screen is the drink, and every word the machine says floats in it on a paper label.
directions.why: It attacks appetite at the root: carbonation is the thing the competition cannot deliver and the thing this machine is built around, so the panel makes effervescence its permanent texture rather than an animation that appears once. It also solves the operation lock and the selection with the same instrument — a liquid line — which is why it can drop both the badge and the bubble loop. The cost is that a tinted ground and a fixed cream label are two palettes running at once, and everything legible has to live on the label, which constrains how much can be on a screen.
directions.references: The pour shot in every soda ad; the inside wall of a just-poured glass, where bubbles cling to the glass and to the ice; old fountain syrup-line sight tubes; bottle labels as objects that float on a coloured body — Orangina, Jarritos, Topo Chico.
directions.palette: background #0d1013 (headspace — the empty glass above the line), surface #f6f1e7 (the label: the opaque cream card every word lives on), surface-alt #1b2a24 (liquid depth, for tracks and wells), accent #f2b705 (bubble gold), secondary — the liquid body, tinted per channel and shipped as --liq-a #3d1020 and --liq-b #17402c, text #10120f (on labels), text-dim #6b6a5f, good #45c27d, warn #f2853f
directions.typography: Fraunces 700 (opsz 72, SOFT 50) for titles and numerals — the ratio at 64px, page and lock titles at 34–40px. Figtree 500/700 for labels and body — labels 20px 700 uppercase 0.1em, body 22px 500. Fraunces is soft, slightly wonky and edible rather than corporate, which is what keeps a dark liquid panel from reading as industrial; its rule is that it only ever sets on a cream label, never on the liquid. Figtree on liquid is always cream and always 700.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps 190/610 and rotates what the rail means: it is the left wall of the glass, the same liquid, with a 2px cream hairline at x 189 and no card behind any item. The four destinations are 44px cream icons over cream Figtree 700 20, drawn directly on the liquid; the active one is an opaque 174×110 cream label with liquid-coloured text and icon. The whole direction runs on one rule a builder can apply anywhere: cream is a label, everything else is liquid.
directions.selectionDevice: The liquid line. One hard horizontal edge crosses the pane at pane-content y 168 — below it is the selected channel's tint with bubbles rising through it, above it is #0d1013 headspace with none. The selected flavor's card is submerged: its cream label sits in the tint with a 6px column of bubbles climbing its left edge. The unselected flavor's card is above the line on #0d1013, dry — its face washed 45% flat toward #0d1013, its numerals #6b6a5f. Tap it and the line moves to put it under. One is wet and one is dry.
directions.faceTreatment: A face is a paper label on a bottle: 43:80 at 129×240 on Choose, centred on the cream card with a 2px #10120f keyline and a 10px cream margin, 172×320 on the anchored pages, 86×160 in the picker and the lock. A submerged face carries six bubble rings clinging to the outside of its keyline — the ones that stick to the inside of the glass. The picker strip is a cream band floating across the liquid, its chosen tile lifted 8px with a 3px #f2b705 ring. Bubbles are never alpha and never blurred: hard-edged 1px rings at 3, 5 and 8px in three flat depth colours — near #f2b705, mid #7f8f5a, far #33452f — about seventy of them, denser at the bottom, none in the top 40px of the liquid.
directions.lockTreatment: The glass fills, and the fill is the progress bar. The whole 800×480 is the glass: at 40% the liquid line sits at y 288, tint below it, headspace above, bubbles rising only in the tint. The channel's 172×320 face stands at x 48 half submerged — full colour below the line, washed flat toward #0d1013 above it, with the line crossing the artwork crisply at full width. The cream modal label floats at (360, 130), 380×220: Cleaning in Fraunces 700 40, 1 of 3 · water in in Figtree 500 22 #6b6a5f, 11 MIN LEFT in Figtree 700 20 #f2853f, and STOP as a 140×56 plate in the channel's liquid colour with cream text at the label's bottom right. No bar, no percentage — the bar is 800px wide and it is the drink. Still frame: line at y 288.
directions.risks: A line that rises a few pixels a minute can read as a frozen screen, so the bubble field has to keep moving even when the line does not — drop the 10fps loop and this lock loses its only motion. Two palettes run at once and the cream label must never take the channel's tint, or the one reliably legible surface on the panel moves with the flavor. 3px bubble rings are at the floor of what survives RGB565 and kitchen glare at arm's length, so nothing at that size may carry meaning. And half-submerging someone else's logo is a treatment applied to artwork the direction does not control: if the line is not crisp, full width and perfectly horizontal, it reads as a rendering fault rather than a pour.

directions.name: Process Line
directions.thesis: There is a real fluid path behind this glass — cold line, carbonator, two pumps, valves, faucet — and the panel's job is to show you which part of it is open, so every screen carries the plant mimic and a selection is a valve that is actually shut.
directions.why: Attacks the honesty pressure head-on: the selection is not a badge invented for the UI, it is the state of a valve, and the reservoir gauge is the same four stations as the four reeds in Settings, so Choose and Settings become one drawing at two zooms. It buys a person an accurate mental model of their own appliance in the time it takes to pour a glass. It costs pixels — a 64 px mimic strip on every page — and it demands ruthless editing, because a mimic that grows tags and instrument bubbles becomes the builder's screen.
directions.references: ISA-101 high-performance HMI (grey ground, colour reserved for state), Rational combi-oven service graphics, brewery and dairy CIP panels, Siemens WinCC mimics done well, Decent DE1 pressure/flow pages, Beck and Vignelli diagrammatic line work.
directions.palette: background #0e1417 (graphite), surface #182126 (page body panel), surface-alt #222d33 (well, closed valve, unlit leg), accent #2fb7c8 (the open path, and only the open path), secondary #7d8c94 (pipe and vessel line work), text #e7eff2, text-dim #93a4ac, good #4cbf72 (a reed closed, a level proved), warn #f0a02a (level low, refusal). Line weights: 2 px idle pipe, 5 px flowing leg, 3 px vessel wall.
directions.typography: Barlow Semi Condensed 600 for caps labels at 20 px, tracked +0.06em, and 500 at 24 px for sentence text; Roboto Mono 500 tabular for every figure — ratio 56 px, countdown 44 px, level stations 20 px. Condensed caps are what fits beside a pipe without crowding it; the mono keeps a changing number from shifting its neighbours.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190 px rail and re-reads it as the trunk: a 4 px #7d8c94 vertical line at x 178 runs the rail's full height with a tap stub into each of the four 110 px destinations, so CHOOSE·PRIME·FILL·CLEAN read as four take-offs in order of destructiveness. The active destination's stub and the trunk above it go #2fb7c8 and its plate fills #222d33. The pane gains a persistent 610×64 mimic strip at its top — carbonator, tee, two channel pumps, faucet — identical on every page, with only the lit leg changing; the page body sits beneath it. Settings is a 56×56 outlined square in the mimic strip's right end, drawn as an instrument tap off the line rather than a button.
directions.selectionDevice: In the mimic strip the selected channel's leg is a 5 px #2fb7c8 line running reservoir → pump → tee → faucet, and the other channel's leg is a 2 px #7d8c94 line broken by a filled valve symbol — a closed valve, which is the machine's actual state. On Choose the selected card additionally takes a 6 px #2fb7c8 edge down its west side; the unselected card keeps a 2 px #222d33 edge. Nothing else on a normal screen is saturated, so the open path is the only colour in the room.
directions.faceTreatment: The face lives inside its vessel. A 43:80 tank outline in 3 px #7d8c94 with a 4 px corner radius, the face inset 4 px so the picture is the liquid in the tank; up the tank's outer wall runs a scale with four tick stations — the same 57.5 / 102.5 / 147.5 / 192.5 reeds Settings draws — and a level line drawn across the tank at the current station, #4cbf72, or #f0a02a with a LOW flag at station one. 129×240 on Choose, 172×320 on a flavour page, 86×160 on the lock. The eight-face row is eight bare 86×160 faces on a pipe-like 4 px track; the chosen one is tapped off it with a 5 px cyan stub.
directions.lockTreatment: The mimic goes full screen and becomes the cycle's own drawing: tap water in → idle pump → reservoir → dispense path → faucet → pitcher, with the leg that is flowing right now drawn 5 px #2fb7c8 carrying four 12 px chevrons along it (one still frame of the marching flow every process panel animates), every other leg 2 px #7d8c94. Beneath it a three-round ladder as three pairs of boxes, IN / OUT, the current box filled #2fb7c8 with 1 OF 3 · WATER IN beside it, a 610×8 progress rule at 40%, and 11 MIN LEFT in Roboto Mono 44 right-aligned. The channel's tank sits at the left. STOP is a 220×96 target with a 4 px #f0a02a border on #182126 — the only hard-edged warm thing on the panel.
directions.risks: The whole direction lives one bad decision from the debug screen: no tag numbers, no pressures, no PID bubbles, no valve designators — the diagram may only show plumbing the owner can point at. Chevrons and 1 px hairlines disappear at arm's length and under RGB565's coarse steps in dark greys (#182126 and #222d33 are barely two steps apart in red and blue — verify on glass). Cyan on graphite can look cold and clinical beside warm kitchen lighting. And a mimic strip repeated on five pages becomes furniture if it never changes; if a page cannot light a different leg, that page should not carry it.

directions.name: Two Channel
directions.thesis: The machine has exactly two channels and one timebase, and a measuring instrument already has a language for that: channel colours that never change, a graticule everything sits on, and a cursor that says where in the run you are.
directions.why: Attacks the hardest requirement in the brief — that a channel is named by its face and never by a number — by giving each channel a colour that is carried on every screen, so identity is visual and absolute without a letter or a digit anywhere. It buys the lock screen the best structure of the five: the cycle drawn on a real time axis with the three rounds as labelled segments on it. It costs warmth, and it is the direction with the shortest distance to the forbidden look, so the discipline against instrument furniture has to be total.
directions.references: Tektronix and Keysight bench scopes (soft keys down the right of the CRT, channel-coloured everything), Teenage Engineering OP-1 colour coding, HP test-gear faceplates, La Marzocco Leva's shot-clock, analyser waterfall displays, oscillograph paper.
directions.palette: background #0a0d0c, surface #111614 (the graticule field), surface-alt #1a211e (a well or a dead soft key), accent #ffb000 (CHANNEL A, amber), secondary #29d4e8 (CHANNEL B, cyan), text #d8e4de, text-dim #6e837a, good #5ce07a, warn #ff6a3d. Graticule lines #24302b at 1 px, axis lines #35453e at 1 px with 5 sub-ticks per division.
directions.typography: JetBrains Mono 400/700 tabular for every readout — ratio 72 px, countdown 44 px, measurement badges 24 px — and Archivo Narrow 600 caps at 20 px, tracked +0.05em, for soft-key labels and page names. Mono for facts, narrow caps for the keys: the same split a bench instrument makes between what it measures and what it is told.
directions.layoutMove: Moves the rail to the RIGHT edge as a 190 px soft-key column of four 110 px keys, and gives the pane the left 610 px as the graticule field. The move earns itself twice: the face is the name, so the faces must be the first thing a left-to-right scan meets, and the keys land under the hand of someone standing over the cabinet rather than across their reach. The graticule is 10 × 8 divisions of 61 × 56 px and every block on every page is a whole number of divisions wide and tall — no element floats. Settings takes the graticule's top-left corner as a 56×56 outlined square, the position a scope gives acquisition status, and never touches the key column.
directions.selectionDevice: Intensity, the way a scope shows the active channel: the selected flavour's block is drawn at full brightness with a 3 px channel-coloured rule down its west edge and a 44 px filled channel-colour square at its top-right; the unselected block — face, figures, rules and all — is drawn at 35% and its edge rule is #1a211e. A measurement badge at the graticule's top-left carries the selected channel's ratio in that channel's own colour, so the panel states its selection twice, once by brightness and once by where the bright colour is.
directions.faceTreatment: 129×240 on Choose, 172×320 on a flavour page, 86×160 on the lock, each in a 2 px frame of its channel's colour with a 12 px flag notched into the frame's top-left — the channel marker a scope puts at the left of its trace. The unselected face's frame drops to 35%. The eight-face row is drawn as a record of waveform memories: 86×160 faces on the division grid with a full-width 4 px #1a211e line beneath them and a bright channel-coloured segment over the part of the record currently on screen, which is the honest form of both the scrollbar and the position indicator.
directions.lockTreatment: The key column stays, and every key but one goes dark #1a211e with its label at #6e837a — the lock is the machine refusing every input, drawn as dead keys, and STOP is the single live key, filled #ff6a3d at the column's foot. The graticule field carries the cycle on a real time axis: 0 to 11 MIN across 10 divisions with tick labels, the elapsed region filled channel-amber to 40%, a 2 px vertical cursor at the head with a flag reading 11 MIN LEFT, and the three rounds as three labelled segments along the axis itself — 1 WATER IN bright, 2 and 3 at 35% — so the ladder and the bar are one object rather than two. The channel's face stands at the left in its coloured frame. The only motion is the cursor, advancing a pixel about every 2.7 s.
directions.risks: This is the direction that becomes a debug screen if anything leaks: no timebase, no volts/div, no trigger legend, no sample counter, no grid coordinates — if a label would only mean something to the person who built the machine, it is out. A 1 px graticule on near-black is the first casualty of kitchen glare and of RGB565's coarse dark steps; consider 2 px on the axes only. The 35% dim state can be misread as disabled rather than unselected, so the bright channel must also be the one holding the colour badge. And amber-plus-cyan on black is unmistakably test equipment — in a kitchen that is either the point or the objection.

directions.name: Flap Board
directions.thesis: This machine keeps a roll-call of its own state, and the panel is the mechanical board that posts it — a grid of character cells that flip when the truth changes, so a change is an event rather than a repaint.
directions.why: Attacks readability and presence together: a cell grid forces the direction to say almost nothing, in caps, at 40 px, which is exactly what a person wanting a Diet Mountain Dew can read from the doorway. It buys the appliance a piece of furniture-grade character that no competitor's screen has, and it makes the selected flavour a solid bar of colour four cells long. It costs flexibility — every string must fit its cells — and it forbids fine detail, so the reed diagram has to be drawn inside a cell block rather than freely.
directions.references: Vestaboard, Solari di Udine split-flap departure boards, Teenage Engineering's cell-based legends, Braun's flip clocks, letterpress chase and slug composition, the Swiss railway's character-cell timetables.
directions.palette: background #100f0d (board matte), surface #1a1916 (cell face), surface-alt #262420 (the upper flap half, one step lighter so the seam reads), accent #e2521f (orange chip), secondary #c8a44c (brass chip, for a value under attention), text #efe7d6 (ivory character), text-dim #8a8376, good #4c9f5a (green chip), warn #e0a92b (yellow chip). Chips are flat cell fills with dark #100f0d characters on them; there are exactly five chip colours and no others.
directions.typography: DM Mono 500, caps only, one family for the whole direction. 40 px in a full cell, 20 px for the rare sub-label that shares a cell row. Letter spacing is the grid itself — one glyph per cell — so figures are tabular by construction and a ratio changing from 1:20 to 1:14 moves nothing.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the skeleton by rebuilding it as one board: 25 columns × 8 rows of 32×60 px cells across the whole 800×480, 1 px #100f0d gutters. The rail is columns 1–6 (192 px, the current 190 within a pixel) — each destination is a two-row block of six cells, CHOOSE / PRIME / FILL / CLEAN set in them, and the pane is columns 7–25 (608 px). Every cell carries a 1 px #2c2a25 seam across its horizontal midline: the flap split, and the direction's signature. Settings is a single cell in the board's top-right corner bearing a gear glyph on the cell ground — one cell against a destination's twelve, which is the whole argument for its rank.
directions.selectionDevice: The selected flavour's title row flips to chips: a run of orange #e2521f cells with dark characters, spanning that flavour's full block width. The unselected flavour's title row stays ivory-on-cell. A solid bar of orange four to six cells long is legible across a kitchen, and it is the same device a board uses for the boarding flight.
directions.faceTreatment: A face occupies a block of cells — 4 cols × 4 rows = 128×240 on Choose, 5×5 = 160×300 scaled to a 43:80 crop on a flavour page, 3×3 on the lock — and the cell gutters and midline seams are drawn OVER the picture at 18% ivory, so the image is behind the flaps and the board is never broken by a photograph. The eight-face row is a single row of 3-cell blocks that runs off the board's right edge; a 1-cell arrow chip at each end pages it, and the row beneath shows position as filled versus empty cells.
directions.lockTreatment: The board dims to bare cell ground except a three-row banner. Row 1: CLEANING in orange chips, with the channel's face block at the left. Row 2: a 19-cell progress run where a completed step is an orange chip and the rest are cell ground — at 40%, eight chips; the cell at the head of the run is drawn mid-flip, its upper half showing the next chip's colour and its lower half the old, which is the one moving element and needs no loop to read as motion. Row 3: 11 MIN LEFT at the left, 1 OF 3 WATER IN at the right, and STOP as a four-cell run of white chips with dark characters. Nothing else on the board is chipped, so STOP is the only white on the panel.
directions.risks: A cell grid is expensive in space: the reed side-profile in Settings must live inside a 12×5 cell block and will lose fine stations, so the drawing has to be redrawn at cell resolution rather than shrunk. 1 px seams over a photographic face can moiré once RGB565 quantizes them; test the seam at 12% and 18%. The conceit slides from machine-true to retro-cute the moment a fifth or sixth chip colour appears or a cell animates for decoration. And all-caps mono is slow to read in quantity — any page needing a sentence is a page this direction has got wrong.

directions.name: Broadsheet
directions.thesis: The panel is a printed page and not a screen: the machine's state is set in type at a size you read from across the room, and the faces are plates in the column.
directions.why: This is the almost-entirely-typographic direction. It attacks the inverted hierarchy head-on — on a page, importance is size, and size is absolute, so 'which flavor is armed' can be four times the area of 'what ratio it pours at' with no colour doing any work at all. It buys a panel with no card chrome to get wrong and no icon set to draw badly, which is the fastest route out of the LVGL-symbol tell. It costs the panel its affordances: on a page nothing looks pressable, so every target has to be given a printed press state and a generous invisible hit region, and the design has to be policed hard or it becomes a poster you cannot operate.
directions.references: Monocle and Apartamento's column rules, Wallpaper* department pages, Penguin and Faber jacket typography, Massimo Vignelli's grid work, Japanese instruction inserts, museum wall labels, the specimen sheets of a type foundry.
directions.palette: background #f6f3ec (newsprint), surface #f6f3ec — the page has no cards, so surface and ground are one colour and this is the point, surface-alt #ebe6da (the single tint block, used for a pressed state and nothing else), accent #b3301c (one vermilion, used only on the selected rule and on STOP), secondary #1b1a17 (ink, which does almost all the structural work), text #1b1a17, text-dim #6f6a5f, good #2d6a4a, warn #9a6510.
directions.typography: Two families, split by size. Instrument Serif 400 (and its italic) for display only, at 64, 96 and 220 — its hairlines need the size, so nothing under 48px is ever set in it, which is a hard rule on this panel. Inter Tight 500 and 700 for everything at or under 28: legends in caps at 20/22 with 0.12em tracking, captions at 20, the running note at 22. Numerals ride tabular figures in Inter Tight where they change (ratio, level) and Instrument Serif where they are the headline (the minutes on the lock). Three type sizes on any one screen, never four.
directions.layoutMove: Dissolves the rail into a masthead, and this is the direction's structural argument: the content unit is 43:80 and the panel is 1.67:1, so 190px of permanent left-hand furniture is taken out of the one dimension the faces need. CHOOSE · PRIME · FILL · CLEAN become four 200×92 typographic slots across the top of the page, y 0–92, divided by 1px ink hairlines, each an Inter Tight 700 22px caps word over a 32px ink-stroked mark; the one you are on carries an 8px solid ink bar along its bottom edge. A 2px ink rule at y 92 is the masthead rule. The page below is 800×388 with 32px margins and a 24px gutter, and Settings is a 20px caps word set flush right in the masthead's own baseline — smaller than every destination, which is the hierarchy claim made typographically. Square corners everywhere; paper does not round.
directions.selectionDevice: Rank on the page. The selected flavor is set as the lead item: its face at 172×320 flush left at full ink, above a 10px solid ink rule that runs the width of its column, with 1:20 in Instrument Serif 96 and LEVEL 3 OF 4 in 20px caps beneath. The unselected flavor is the second item: its face at 86×160 — one quarter the area — printed at a flat 55% ink coverage over paper, under a 1px hairline, with 1:14 at 40px and LEVEL 1 OF 4 · LOW in vermilion caps. Size, ink coverage and rule weight all say the same thing three ways, and there is no badge, no outline and no fill anywhere.
directions.faceTreatment: A plate in a column. Every face is a 43:80 rectangle with a 1px ink hairline and a caption set directly under it in 20px caps — the figure-caption relationship, not a card. Scales are 172×320 (lead), 129×240 (pick screens and picker), 86×160 (the demoted item and the lock). The pick screens give each channel a full half-column: face at 172×320 flush to the column's west edge, the funnel drawn as a 48px ink figure directly above it, and the whole half-column pressable — the plate IS the target, which is what finally uses the 43:80's width instead of padding it inside a landscape box. The pressed state is a 2px ink border drawn inside the plate's own hairline, shown on this study's pick.html.
directions.lockTreatment: The page reverses to ink: full-bleed #1b1a17, everything paper-coloured. No animation — a page does not move, it is reprinted. 11 in Instrument Serif 220 flush left at x 40, MIN LEFT in Inter Tight 700 28 caps set on its baseline to the right; CLEANING as a running head at 32 caps above; 1 OF 3 · WATER IN at 22 caps at 70% paper. Progress is one 24px paper bar across x 40→760 with a vermilion #b3301c fill to 40% and 1px ink ticks at the thirds. The face at 129×240, paper-hairlined, flush right at x 631. STOP is a 280×110 solid paper block with ink Inter Tight 700 32 caps, bottom-right — the only paper-filled object on the ink field.
directions.risks: The palest ground of the five and therefore the worst night lamp; the mitigation is the sheer area of 220px black display type and the ink-reversed lock, but Choose at 2am is a bright rectangle and this direction has to own that. Instrument Serif's hairlines will drop out entirely on RGB565 below about 40px and will alias on the panel's unfiltered grid even at 96 — the ≥48px rule is load-bearing, and the device build needs the serif hinted or rendered at 2× and downsampled into the font image. The 55% ink-coverage face must be a baked second asset, not a runtime opacity blend, or the framebuffer cost lands on every selection change. Biggest risk is operability: with no fills and no chrome, a first-time user may not know the plates are targets — the printed press state and a 64px minimum hit region around every word are not optional here.

directions.name: Enamel Plate
directions.thesis: The panel is a piece of enamelware — a cream field bounded by hard cobalt ink, where everything is either printed on the enamel or is a chip of colour laid into it.
directions.why: Attacks the selection failure and the dev-tool icon vocabulary at once. Enamel signage has exactly one move — knock the ground out and fill it with ink — so 'this flavor is the one' becomes a value inversion (cream card vs. cobalt card, roughly 15:1) instead of the current 1.26:1 shade step, and the mark system has an obvious house style to be drawn in: single-weight 4px strokes, flat terminals, no FontAwesome anywhere. It costs the machine its neutrality — cobalt and enamel red are an opinion in a kitchen, and a buyer who wanted stainless-and-nothing will notice. It also spends its accent budget early, so nothing else on the panel may be red.
directions.references: Falcon Enamelware, Dansk Købenstyle, French emaillerie street signs and cartouches, Le Creuset and Descoware colourways, vintage Belgian and Dutch enamel advertising plates, Zip HydroTap's printed faceplates.
directions.palette: background #f2ece0 (cream enamel), surface #fbf7ef (the whiter chip a card is struck from), surface-alt #e2d9c6 (a recessed or unavailable field), accent #c8102e (enamel red — commit and the selection stripe only), secondary #18458f (cobalt — rail slab, keylines, masthead, the selected card's ground), text #16233b, text-dim #6d7a90, good #2f7d55, warn #d8862a.
directions.typography: Archivo (Google) at 500, 600 and 800 and nothing else. Legends and captions: Archivo 600 all-caps 20px, letter-spacing 0.08em. Page names: Archivo 800 28px caps. Numbers and the words on the lock: Archivo 800 at 44 and 64. Hierarchy is carried by weight jumps of two steps (500→800) rather than by colour, so the dim tier finally means 'caption', not 'everything small'. Ratio drops to 28px on Choose and only goes to 64 on the flavor's own page, where changing it is the reason you are there.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190 + 610 skeleton and rematerialises it. The rail becomes one full-bleed cobalt slab, x 0–190, no gaps and no card fills — four 190×120 compartments divided by 2px cream rules, legends knocked out in cream, the one you are on a solid cream chip carrying cobalt type. The pane is cream, with one 3px cobalt rule under the page name running x 206→784 as a shared datum: rail top rule, pane rule and the Settings chip's top edge all land on y 76. Radii drop from 14 to 6 — enamel edges are hard. Settings becomes a 64×64 cream chip with a cobalt 4px-stroke mark, sitting on the cobalt slab's top-right corner rather than floating over the pane.
directions.selectionDevice: Inversion plus a stripe. The selected flavor card is a solid cobalt #18458f field, 281×300, with a 3px cream keyline and a 12px enamel-red bar inlaid down its full west edge; all its type is knocked out cream. The unselected card is cream #fbf7ef with a 2px cobalt keyline and no stripe. Both boxes are the same rect at the same coordinates, so nothing moves when the selection does — only the ground changes material. Photographed from two metres and thresholded, one card is black and the other is white.
directions.faceTreatment: 43:80 at 129×240 on Choose, 172×320 on the anchor column, 86×160 in the picker — the existing three scales, each in a 4px keyline that reads as the chip's rim: cream keyline when the face sits on cobalt, cobalt keyline when it sits on cream. Faces are never tinted or scrimmed; the ink belongs to the enamel, the product keeps its own colour. On the pick screens the card is the face's own shape — a 172×320 face, edge to edge inside its keyline, with the funnel mark as a 56px cream-stroked figure on a cobalt header band across the card's top, so there is no half-empty landscape box.
directions.lockTreatment: The one dark screen in the system: full-bleed cobalt, all 800×480. No bubble loop. The face at 172×320 with a cream keyline at x 40; CLEANING in Archivo 800 64px knocked out in cream; 11 MIN LEFT in Archivo 800 44px enamel red directly under it; 1 OF 3 · WATER IN at 20px caps cream at 70% coverage. The progress is a single 18px-tall enamel-red rule running x 252→760 over a cream track, 40% filled, with two 3px cream ticks at the thirds so the three rounds are visible. STOP is a 260×104 solid cream chip with cobalt Archivo 800 28px caps, bottom-right at (500, 336) — the only cream-filled object on the field, so the exit is the most findable thing on the screen and the commit/abort ratio inverts.
directions.risks: Cream at 800×480 with the backlight hard on is a lamp in a dark kitchen; the 190px cobalt slab plus the cobalt rule and keylines hold the mean down, and the lock going full cobalt means the one screen that runs at 2am is the dark one — but Choose at night is still bright, and that has to be accepted as the trade. Enamel red #c8102e sits close to flavor_1's crimson field; never put the red stripe adjacent to a face, keep it inboard on the cobalt. Cobalt-on-cream is a huge value jump and 565 handles both as flat fills, but the 2px cream keylines on cobalt will alias on the panel's own grid — spec them at 3px on the device. Cream also shows fingerprints in the sense that any smudge on the glass reads against a light ground far more than against #1a1a2e; that is a real kitchen-appliance cost.

directions.name: Soft Clay
directions.thesis: The panel is a ceramic tile set into the cabinet face, and the two flavors are objects on it — one picked up, one set down.
directions.why: Attacks selection and press feedback with physics instead of colour: raised versus pressed is a difference of object class, not of shade, and it reads from two metres without spending the accent. It is also the only direction here that answers 'what should a quiet appliance look like when it is doing nothing', which is what this panel is doing 99% of the time — warm, matte, unlit, furniture. The cost is that softness and RGB565 are enemies: every rounded corner staircases and every shadow has to be a flat offset band, so the direction survives only under strict rules. It is also the palest at rest and the most at risk of washing out.
directions.references: Muji's kitchen appliances and CD player, Hay and Ferm Living tableware, Jasper Morrison for Rowenta, Naoto Fukasawa's humidifiers, Heath Ceramics glazes, Tsubame-Sanjo enamel and stoneware, Zojirushi's softer product lines.
directions.palette: background #ebe4d8 (oat — deliberately not white), surface #f7f2e9 (a raised body), surface-alt #ddd4c4 (a well, a recess, a pressed-in object), accent #c2603f (terracotta — the pour, the commit, the lock's ground), secondary #6f8a7a (sage — quiet structure, rims, the running state), text #33302b, text-dim #8a8176, good #4b7f5c, warn #cf9339. One extra named tone the builder needs: shadow #d6ccba, used only as a flat 4px offset band and never as a gradient.
directions.typography: Zen Maru Gothic (Google) 500 and 700 for everything — a rounded humanist gothic whose numerals are round enough to belong to the ceramic register and heavy enough at 700 to hold at two metres. Legends at 20 caps with 0.06em tracking in 500; card headings at 26 in 700; the ratio at 40 on Choose and 64 on the flavor's own page; the lock's verb at 64. Where roundness softens too far — the small caps legends on Settings and the lock's note — swap to Zen Kaku Gothic New 500 at 22, same family designer, flatter terminals. Nothing under 20.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190 + 610 skeleton and rebuilds both halves as materials. The rail becomes a recess: a surface-alt well inset 8px on all sides with a 2px #cfc5b3 line along its north and west (a drawn inset, no blur), holding four 160×96 pebbles at 28px radius — the current one raised in surface #f7f2e9 with its mark in terracotta and a 4px shadow band, the others flush in the well with sage marks. Pane padding goes from 16 to 24 and card radii from 14 to 28; the gutter between the two Choose cards goes from 16 to 24. Everything gets more air and fewer edges. Settings is a 64×64 pebble in the rail well's own bottom corner, sage mark, below the four — physically in the furniture drawer rather than floating over the pane.
directions.selectionDevice: Height. The selected card is raised: surface #f7f2e9, 28px radius, a flat 4px #d6ccba shadow band offset south-east, and a 10px terracotta bar inlaid along its top edge inside the radius. The unselected card is pressed in: surface-alt #ddd4c4 fill, no shadow, a 2px #cfc5b3 inset line along its north and west, and its contents shifted 2px south-east as if they had sunk. Identical rects at identical coordinates — nothing moves, only the object's relationship to the surface. The same raised/pressed pair is the press state everywhere on the panel, so touching anything makes it sink, which is the feedback the four zero-feedback buttons never had.
directions.faceTreatment: The face is an inlay. A 43:80 well at 16px radius is cut into the card — 129×240 on Choose, 172×320 on the anchor and pick screens, 86×160 in the picker — with a 3px surface-alt rim all round so it reads as seated in the clay rather than pasted on it. On the pressed card the rim darkens to #cfc5b3 and the face takes a flat 30% oat scrim, baked as a second asset: the drink is put away, not deleted. On the pick screens the card IS the well plus a 56px terracotta-stroked funnel above it, so a 172×320 face owns a 220×420 card and there is no empty half.
directions.lockTreatment: The tile closes. The whole panel floods terracotta #c2603f, and one oat card — 640×360 at (80, 60), 40px radius, no shadow because nothing is above the lock — holds everything: the face inlaid at 86×160 flush west, Cleaning in Zen Maru Gothic 700 64 beside it, 1 of 3 · water in at 22, and the progress as a physical trough — a 28px-tall surface-alt groove at 14px radius with a sage #6f8a7a fill to 40%, drawn with a 2px #cfc5b3 rim so the level reads as liquid standing in a channel. 11 MIN LEFT at 40 in terracotta directly above it. The 16-frame loop is replaced by the trough's level itself, which rises once a minute; draw it as one still at 40%. STOP is a 220×96 solid terracotta pill at 48px radius in the card's south-east — the only terracotta object inside the oat card, so it is the exit by material as well as by position.
directions.risks: Palest ground of the five at rest and the highest wash-out risk; oat #ebe4d8 rather than white, the surface-alt rail well, and a terracotta lock are the three defences, and if it still reads as a lamp at night the ground drops another step to #e3dbcb before anything else changes. 28px and 40px radii on RGB565 with no anti-aliasing will staircase visibly at arm's length — every rounded shape needs a 2px rim one step darker than its fill to absorb the jaggies, and that rim is part of the spec. The flat 4px shadow band must never become a blur or it bands. Terracotta and flavor_3's orange collide badly, so a face is never placed on the terracotta field, only inside an oat card. Finally, soft and quiet can tip into vague: the raised/pressed delta has to be checked by thresholding a two-metre photograph, and if it fails, the terracotta top bar on the raised card widens from 10px to 16px.

directions.name: Riso Kitchen
directions.thesis: Two inks on paper — the panel is a screenprinted poster of what the machine is doing, where colour tells you which ink, never which shade.
directions.why: Attacks the palette problem by removing shades from the vocabulary entirely: with two inks and their overprint there are four possible fields, so the accent cannot quietly acquire five jobs the way #e94560 did. It also solves press feedback in a dimension the current palette has run out of — a flat offset misregistration block gives depth and a press state without a single gradient, which is exactly what RGB565 and a dirty-rectangle repaint budget want. The cost is loudness: this is a poster on a kitchen appliance, and it will read as young. The fluorescent pink is also the brightest field any of these five puts on the glass.
directions.references: Risograph print shops (Fluorescent Pink 1004 and Federal Blue), Hato Press and Colorama editions, Swiss and Polish screenprinted posters, Nathalie Du Pasquier, Japanese konbini signage, the two-colour cookbooks of the 1960s.
directions.palette: background #f5eede (paper), surface #efe5cf (the second paper tint, for a quiet block), surface-alt #2b2a58 (the overprint — pink over blue, the darkest field available and the only 'third value'), accent #ff4a7d (fluorescent pink), secondary #2f56c4 (federal blue), text #241f3d, text-dim #7b88c9 (a 50% blue halftone, specified as a flat colour so it never dithers), good #0f9b63 (riso green), warn #ff9a1f (riso orange).
directions.typography: Space Grotesk 700 for every word — page names at 32 caps, card headers at 26, the lock's verb at 72 — and Space Mono 700 for every number and coded legend: 1:20, 3/4, 11 MIN, 1 OF 3. The split is semantic and absolute: prose is grotesk, data is mono. Space Mono's fixed pitch means the ratio and the minutes never reflow as they change, which kills a whole class of repaint jitter. Sizes 20 / 26 / 44 / 72, tracking 0.06em on all caps.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190 + 610 split and floods the rail with ink: x 0–190 is a solid pink field, its four destinations knocked out in paper as 48px marks over 22px caps, and the one you are on is a paper block with pink type. The pane is paper. Two printed devices run through everything: a 2px checkerboard halftone in blue — cells exactly 2px on the panel's own grid, so 565 renders it without a single artefact — used as the fill for any 'partial' quantity, and a 6px offset misregistration block behind every card, a flat duplicate rectangle in the opposite ink with no blur. Cards are paper with a 3px blue keyline. Radius 4, near-square.
directions.selectionDevice: Overprint. The selected flavor card is flooded with pink ink — solid #ff4a7d, a 3px blue keyline, all type knocked out in paper, and its misregistration block flips to blue and grows to 8px. The unselected card is paper with the blue keyline and a 6px pink misregistration block. The ink field versus the paper field is the entire signal, it survives thresholding, and the 2px checkerboard reappears as the level gauge inside both cards — four cells, lit ones solid ink, unlit ones halftone — so 'how much syrup is left' is drawn in the same printed language as everything else.
directions.faceTreatment: Each face sits in a paper window with a 3px blue keyline, 129×240 on Choose and 172×320 on the pick screens and anchor, with a 40px ink header bar knocked out across the window's top carrying the ratio in Space Mono 26 — pink bar with paper type on the selected card, blue bar with paper type elsewhere. The face itself is never tinted, scrimmed or halftoned: the inks belong to the paper, and the product's own colour is the one thing the poster does not print over. A 3px paper gutter always separates a face from any pink field so flavor_1's crimson cannot vibrate against the fluorescent.
directions.lockTreatment: The whole page floods pink, 800×480, and the cycle is drawn as a print run. CLEANING at Space Grotesk 700 72 knocked out in paper, top-left at (40, 48). The progress is a 40px-tall blue bar across x 40→760 at y 300, filled to 40%, with paper registration ticks at the thirds and the unfilled remainder in the 2px blue checkerboard so 'printed' and 'still to print' are two textures, not two shades. 11 MIN on a 220×80 paper chip in blue Space Mono 44, at (40, 210). The face at 129×240 flush right with a paper keyline. The moving element is replaced by a still 200px column of rising 2px-checkerboard bubbles up the left margin — texture, not animation, and nothing repaints at 10fps. STOP is a 300×110 solid blue block with paper Space Grotesk 700 32 caps and an 8px pink misregistration offset, bottom-centre at (250, 350) — the largest object under the bar.
directions.risks: A full-field fluorescent pink at night is the brightest thing in this study and there is no dimming; the lock is the screen most likely to be up at an odd hour, so this may need the flood inverted to blue on the device. The halftone is only safe at exactly 2px on the panel's native grid — at --dpr 2 in the study it must be authored as 4px so it lands on 2 real pixels, and any scaling will moiré. Pink #ff4a7d against flavor_1's #8c1030 field is a vibrating edge at arm's length; the 3px paper gutter is mandatory, not stylistic. Space Mono's fixed pitch is wide — check that 1 OF 3 · WATER IN fits its column before committing the size. And the whole register risks reading as a student poster rather than a $7,500 appliance: the discipline that saves it is that every ink field is a semantic state, never decoration.

directions.name: Legend Plate
