directions.thesis: The panel is the appliance's own silkscreened faceplate — printed legend on warm plastic, dark recessed windows where the information lives, and exactly one lamp lit.
directions.why: The only direction that is light without being pale: a light plate with dark wells inverts the night problem, because the bright area is furniture and the glowing area is small and intentional. It attacks the icon tell by adopting a vocabulary that has no icons at all — a faceplate prints words, tick marks and segment bars — and it solves selection with the most literal appliance signal that exists, a lit lamp, which cannot be mistaken for a shade. It costs charm: this is the least domestic of the five and the most likely to read as equipment rather than furniture, which is exactly the accusation the current dark design already faces, so it has to be warm plastic and not grey.
directions.references: Zojirushi and Panasonic rice cooker faceplates, Braun's Dieter Rams control panels, Teenage Engineering OP-1's printed legends, Miele's silkscreened fascias, aviation annunciator panels, Japanese washing-machine legends, Bang & Olufsen's aluminium legend plates.
directions.palette: background #d9d5cc (warm plastic plate), surface #c9c4b8 (a moulded compartment on the plate), surface-alt #23262a (a recessed window — the only dark field, and always bounded), accent #ff7a18 (the lamp, and the only saturated hue on the plate), secondary #4a5560 (printed legend ink), text #21252a, text-dim #6d7580, good #17a35c (a green lamp), warn #e0a020. Two more the builder needs for the moulding: highlight #f0ece2 and groove #a9a396, used as a 1px pair to draw every engraved line.
directions.typography: IBM Plex Sans 600 for printed legends, always caps, 20–22px, letter-spacing 0.14em — that tracking is the faceplate's signature and is not optional. IBM Plex Sans Condensed 600 22 for the four rail legends, so CHOOSE, PRIME, FILL and CLEAN sit at real size inside 190px. IBM Plex Mono 600 and 700 for every number without exception — 1:20, 3 OF 4, 11, 1 OF 3 — at 24 inside a card and 96 inside the lock's window, because a faceplate numbers things in fixed pitch and a monospaced readout never reflows as it counts down. Prose does not exist on this panel; everything is a legend or a number.
directions.layoutMove: Keeps the 190px rail's width and removes its fills entirely. Each destination becomes a moulded compartment — a 178×110 rounded rect at 8px radius drawn as a 2px #a9a396 groove with a 1px #f0ece2 highlight beneath it, no fill, the plate showing through — with its mark printed in #4a5560 at 2px stroke and its legend in condensed caps. The one you are on is marked by a 14px amber lamp disc inset on the compartment's west edge and its legend stepping from #6d7580 to #21252a; no fill changes at all. The pane's content lives in windows: a flavor is a #23262a well with a 2px #b3ad9f engraved rim, set into the plate. Rail groove, pane window and the Settings compartment all share one 2px groove weight and one y-76 datum. Settings is a 64×64 compartment on the plate at (720, 16) with a printed legend beneath it at 18px caps — smaller than any rail legend, which is the hierarchy claim.
directions.selectionDevice: The lamp, as an appliance does it. Each flavor window carries a 24×24 lamp at its top-right: the selected one is a solid #ff7a18 disc inside a 6px #ffd6b0 flat ring — a halo drawn as a second ring, never a blur — and the whole window sits at #23262a with its face at full colour and its printed legend above it in solid #21252a. The unselected window's lamp is an unlit #3a3f45 disc with a 2px #565d66 rim, the window lifts to #2c3036, its face takes a flat 40% plate scrim, and its legend drops to #6d7580. Lit versus unlit is binary by construction and photographs as such; the scrim gives the two-metre read even if the lamp is missed.
directions.faceTreatment: The face finally owns its container. A window is the 43:80 rectangle plus a 40px mono readout strip beneath it and nothing else — the face bleeds to the window's rim on three sides with no padding, at 129×240 on Choose, 172×320 on the pick screens and anchor, 86×160 in the picker and on the lock. The readout strip carries 1:20 · 3 OF 4 in Plex Mono 24 in plate-white on the dark well, and the level is four 28×10 amber-or-unlit cells at its right end — a segment bar, not a gauge. Because the window's outline IS the face's aspect, none of the three scales sits inside a landscape box anywhere on the panel.
directions.lockTreatment: The plate stays and the pane becomes one window: a 736×416 #23262a well at (32, 32) with its engraved rim, CLEANING printed on the plate above it in 28 caps tracked. Inside the well: the face at 129×240 flush west; 11 in Plex Mono 700 at 96 with MIN LEFT at 24 caps on its baseline; 1 OF 3 · WATER IN at 22 caps in #8a929c. The progress is not a bar but a row of thirty discrete 20×28 cells at 6px pitch across the well's width, 12 of them lit amber and the rest at #3a3f45 — a rice cooker's segment graph, which RGB565 renders exactly and which quantises an eleven-minute cycle into something a person can count. The only motion is the leading cell blinking at 1Hz, so the 10fps loop and its 117ms repaint go away entirely. STOP is a 260×96 target on the PLATE, outside the well, bottom-right at (508, 368): plate-coloured with a 4px amber rim and amber Plex Sans 600 32 caps — the exit is physically on the furniture, not inside the machine's own readout, so it is separable at a glance and no longer a tenth of the commit's size.
directions.risks: Dark windows inside a light plate can read as holes rather than displays if the rim contrast is wrong — the #f0ece2 / #a9a396 pair must stay at least three 565 steps apart or the engraved line vanishes and the well looks like a cut-out. The 1px highlight will be invisible on some panel units; if the check photograph loses it, both lines go to 2px and the radius to 10. Amber #ff7a18 sits inside flavor_3's orange family, so a lamp is never placed over a face, only on the plate or on the dark well's own field. Thirty 20px cells at 6px pitch is near the limit of what reads at arm's length; if the two-metre photograph cannot resolve them, drop to fifteen cells at 40px. And the whole register risks reading as equipment rather than kitchen — the defence is that the plate is warm (#d9d5cc, not grey), that there is no grid, no ruler and no telemetry anywhere, and that the only numbers printed are ones the owner actually wants.

dropped.name: Bone Ledger
dropped.thesis: The panel is a printed page from the machine's own manual — warm paper, ink, rules and set type, with nothing on it that a printer could not have printed.

dropped.name: Fountain Counter
dropped.thesis: This is the porcelain-and-chrome counter of a soda fountain: painted enamel signage, printed cards, a syrup sight glass, and a machine that is proud to be a machine in a bright room.

dropped.name: Bench White
dropped.thesis: A machine that does real work has nothing to hide, so the panel is a lit white bench top where the facts are set in type on a grid and nothing is drawn that a rule and a number cannot say.

dropped.name: Machined Face
dropped.thesis: This is not a screen, it is the control plate of an appliance meant to last twenty years, so every element is a part with an edge: keys that light rather than repaint, windows cut through the plate, scales milled into it, and one red button.
